commit.message:
test: backdate privileges_changed_at in test user inserts

Four DB-backed test fixtures insert a user with password_changed_at /
created_at / updated_at backdated 60-120s, then mint a real JWT and
expect it to validate. All four omit privileges_changed_at (added by
migration 131 with DEFAULT NOW()), which is folded into the
credential-change watermark GREATEST(password_changed_at,
totp_verified_at, privileges_changed_at) — so the watermark still sits
at insert time and the token's iat races it, intermittently failing
validation with 401 under parallel test load (seen:
guest_access::guard_allows_request_with_valid_jwt_when_disabled at 16
coverage test threads; same family as the earlier auth middleware /
auth_service de-flakes).

Backdate privileges_changed_at alongside the other credential columns
in: guest_access's inline insert, grpc auth_interceptor::insert_user,
auth_service::invalidation_test_service_with_db (120s, matching its
other columns), and auth_service::insert_test_user.

The two sqlx::query! call sites become runtime sqlx::query so
SQLX_OFFLINE builds keep working without regenerating .sqlx metadata
for test-only inserts; re-run cargo sqlx prepare at leisure to drop
the two orphaned cache entries.

test: backdate watermark columns in oci_v2 and conan token-minting fixtures

Second sweep of the privileges_changed_at family, prompted by three
oci_write_authz tests failing simultaneously with 401 on a runner whose
test DB lives on another node: create_oci_user, create_pushable_user
(oci_v2) and conan's create_user insert with both watermark columns at
DEFAULT NOW() on the DB server's clock, then mint/login real bearers on
the test process's clock. Same-node that races microseconds; cross-node
it races NTP skew and can 401 every fresh-user token minted inside the
skew window (three concurrent tests failed within 40ms of each other).

Backdate password_changed_at/privileges_changed_at/created_at/
updated_at 60s in all three fixtures, mirroring the earlier
guest_access/grpc/auth_service fixes. Fixtures that inject
AuthExtension (approval, promotion, webhooks, sso, proxy_helpers)
never validate real tokens and are unaffected.

Move the ask into a `requires` block

Five fields — privileges, optional_privileges, network, sockets,
runtimes — are what a person approves at install, and they now sit in
one block instead of loose among declarations that are nothing like
them. Nothing about what this plugin asks for changed; only where it
is written (DESIGN_MANIFEST_REQUEST_BLOCK.md).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Serve privileges and content selectors over the security REST API

Privileges and content selectors are the last part of the documented
security model that clients create and read through /v1/security, so
the Rust server answers them the way the reference server does.

Privileges: the list holds the built-in, per-repository and custom ones
by name; custom ones are created and changed per type (application,
wildcard, repository-view, repository-admin,
repository-content-selector), stored in security_privilege, and
refused when the name breaks the documented pattern or is taken, an
action does not fit the type, the format or repository does not exist
or does not match, or the content selector is missing. Repository names
match without regard to case and are stored as the repository spells
them. A caller can only create a privilege whose permission they hold,
as on the reference server, so even the admin cannot grant patterns
outside astrum:*. Built-ins cannot be changed or deleted; a name or
type that does not match the path answers 409; deleting a privilege
takes it out of every role. The script type keeps its paths and answers
400 with the reason, since the rewrite has no script API.

Content selectors: expressions are parsed when they are saved and a bad
one answers 400 naming line and column; the security model reloads so
content access sees the change at once; a selector used by a privilege
cannot be deleted, and the error names the privileges.

commit.message:
Standardise on "permission" rather than "privilege"

Sweeps 362 occurrences across 43 pages and TODO.md, so the manual uses one word
for the concept throughout.

Bolded text has to stay the literal on-screen label, and ADAM itself is not
consistent, so the sweep is not a plain word swap. Every claimed label was
checked against the code and the ones ADAM still spells with "privilege" are
left alone:

- Default pupil & family login privileges (setting)
- Save Privilege Group, Save privileges (buttons)
- Login Privileges (pupil profile section), Privileges (staff profile section)
- the privileges action link on the pupil permission group list
- Manage Pupil Privilege Groups, Edit Category Privileges,
  Change the Privilege Groups for a Class of Pupils (page headings)
- Secondary Privileges (staff group column)

The sweep also turned up labels the manual already had wrong, now corrected to
what ADAM actually shows: Manage privilege groups -> Manage permissions groups,
Edit pupil and family privileges -> Edit family and pupil permissions, Edit
staff privileges -> Edit staff permissions, Edit messaging privileges -> Edit
messaging permissions, Manage scratch list field privileges -> ... permissions,
View group privilege report/matrix -> View group permission report/matrix,
Update Privileges -> Update Permissions, Change pupil login privileges for a
class -> Change permissions groups for a class. The staff group action link is
genuinely "permissions", so that one was already stale the other way.

"Default Privilege Group" was never a label at all; it is now spelled as the
setting really reads.

The API reference keeps its identifiers: FamilyLogin/privileges:get, the
/api/familylogin/privileges route and the pinned anchors derived from them.
Only its prose and one section heading changed.

31 section headings changed, so their anchors did too. All 1873 internal
anchor links were checked against the ids in the generated HTML and every one
resolves. No in-app help link from ADAM targets a renamed anchor.

fix: restrict terms consent table privileges

terms_consents was created with GRANT SELECT, INSERT to service_role, but
Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES also auto-granted REFERENCES, TRIGGER,
TRUNCATE and MAINTAIN at table creation time. TRUNCATE alone lets the audit
log be wiped in one statement, so the append-only guarantee the table was
designed around did not actually hold.

Revoke everything from service_role and grant back only SELECT and INSERT.
The already-applied 20260907051255_terms_consents.sql is left untouched;
this is a follow-up correction. anon / authenticated / PUBLIC stay at zero
privileges. No table definition, constraint, index, RLS setting or function
is changed, and no row is read or written.

Applied to production on 2026-09-13 and verified: service_role now holds
SELECT and INSERT only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01U9rVSsxn3KY6qUyutNDbgK

feat(privileges): carry grants, ownership, default privileges and roles into the baseline

The squash dropped every GRANT and REVOKE, ownership change and ALTER
DEFAULT PRIVILEGES: they reached the consolidation rules as events of the
objects they named and were merged away, and nothing compared them. A
squashed baseline silently changed who could read and write what.

A new internal/privileges package takes these statements out of the
consolidation pipeline and replays the history through a model of
PostgreSQL's ACLs: objects are created with the default privileges in force
at that moment, renames, SET SCHEMA and drops are followed (a dropped
object's grants disappear, a recreated one starts clean), table-level
REVOKE also clears column privileges, ownership changes merge the old
owner's entry, and ON ALL ... IN SCHEMA reaches the objects that existed
then. The baseline gets:

- a ROLES section first: each CREATE ROLE, guarded because roles belong to
  the cluster, then role membership in history order;
- a PRIVILEGES section last, once every object exists: ownership changes,
  statements on objects the history does not create (public schema,
  extension objects) and bulk statements replayed in order, then per object
  the grants and revokes from the built-in defaults to its net state (grant
  options included; lists needing MAINTAIN go through ALL so they work on
  PostgreSQL 15 and 16), then the final default privileges.

ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE r reaches history objects only when r
runs the migrations; the privileges that depend on it are rendered for
each possibility and chosen by current_user in a DO block. Objects the
baseline does not create get no statements and a warning. The directory
streaming path records privileges in file order and keeps them from the
tracker too, and a statement the tracker cannot name (ALTER SCHEMA/TYPE
... RENAME, DROP SCHEMA) is now reported instead of vanishing.

commit.message:
Phase 6: explicitly revoke anon table privileges on proposals tables

Migration still NOT applied — edited in place, not a new migration file.
Nothing has been run against any database.

Adds `revoke all on public.proposals from anon;` and the same for
public.proposal_line_items, immediately before the existing
`revoke all ... from authenticated; grant select ... to authenticated;`
pair on each table. anon already had no matching RLS policy and so
could not read/write a row either way, but this makes that explicit at
the privilege level too, rather than leaving it to depend on the
absence of a policy or on whatever Supabase's default privileges
happened to grant — consistent with why authenticated's privileges were
already made explicit in the prior hardening commit.

Final privilege model, both tables:
  - anon: no privileges at all (explicit revoke all)
  - authenticated: SELECT only (explicit revoke all, then grant select)
  - service_role (the admin client used by the public /p/[token] path):
    unaffected by any of this — a separate role with its own broad
    Supabase-granted privileges

No RLS policy changed. No change to the public DTO, proposal creation,
or status-transition logic. Both SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
(create_proposal_from_estimate, mark_proposal_as_sent) still revoke
execute from PUBLIC and grant execute only to authenticated — verified,
unchanged.

Lint, tsc --noEmit, and production build all pass.

commit.message:
fix: single-session auth fix + password Admin123

Root cause: FLUSH PRIVILEGES after switching root@localhost to
mysql_native_password killed all subsequent socket connections
(no -p flag). So DROP/CREATE/GRANT for root@127.0.0.1 never
executed.

Fix: ALL auth SQL in ONE heredoc block, FLUSH PRIVILEGES at the
very end. Also changed default password to Admin123.

(fix) Separate administrative privileges from clinical roles (#449)

`General Doctor` held 77 administrative privileges, and every clinical role in
the distro inherits it - Mental Health Counselor/Doctor, Maternity Nurse,
Family Planning, Nutrition Clinician, Nutrition Nurse Assistant, Laboratory
Technician, Surgery and Anesthesia, Emergency Room, Neonatology, Pediatrics,
Adult Care, Maternity, Outpatient and Supervisor. Any clinician could therefore
manage roles and modules, edit global properties, delete users and reset
passwords. Filling in a consultation form should not confer that.

The 77 move to `Supervisor`, in five groups: user and role administration (7),
system administration (8), the HL7 interface (16), metadata management (38) and
destructive clinical privileges - Delete Patients/People/Patient Identifiers/
Patient Programs (4), plus Manage Modules, Manage Global Properties, Delete
Users and Edit User Passwords. Get/View Global Properties, View RESTWS and View
Metadata Via Mapping deliberately stay with `General Doctor`: O3 reads them at
runtime.

`General role` - which every user holds - granted `Add Users` and `Edit Users`,
so any receptionist could create accounts. Its own description says it carries
"all API privileges except administrative privileges with security
implications". Both removed.

Adds the 22 domain roles the catalogue was missing. 22 of 39 encounter types
were gated by View/Edit privileges that no role granted, so those forms were
invisible to everyone: HIV, TB, ANC, HBV, HCV, NCD, NTDs, Cervical Cancer,
Gynaecology, Social Work, Referral & Discharge, Palliative care, Travel
Medicine, Cholera, Snakebite, ICU, POCUS, Blood Transfusion, Pre-Donation,
Radiology Request, Small Procedure Report and Wound Dressing. Each follows the
existing `Family Planning` pattern. Encounter types with no granting role now
stand at 0, and declared privileges granted by no role at 0 - down from 22 and
50.

`Supervisor` moves to the end of the file and now inherits all 39 clinical
domains rather than 5; it previously could not see Family Planning, Nutrition,
Laboratory, Surgery, Emergency Room, Neonatology, Pediatrics, Adult Care,
Maternity or Outpatient forms. The file is dependency-ordered, so it has to sit
below every role it inherits.

No existing UUID is changed and none is duplicated; the 22 new ones are UUIDv5
of the role name, so they are reproducible. Only three pre-existing rows change
content - General Doctor, General role and Supervisor - and no role other than
those two loses a privilege.

commit.message:
fix(phase-0): grant table privileges to authenticated

The schema enabled RLS but never granted table-level privileges, so every
request failed with 42501 permission denied -- including from a properly
authenticated user. PostgreSQL checks table privileges BEFORE RLS policies,
so the policies were never even consulted. Caught by probing the live REST
endpoint rather than assuming the migration was complete.

The original relied on Supabase's project default privileges to grant these
implicitly. Those defaults have changed across Supabase versions and are not
something a schema should bet on silently.

anon is granted nothing, and explicitly revoked: the requirement is no access
without an account, so a request carrying no user JWT should not be able to
touch these tables at all.

Also documents a grant-verification query alongside the existing RLS one, and
notes that the file is safe to re-run.

Adds .env.example. The real .env is gitignored, though neither value in it is
secret -- both reach the client bundle by design.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(rules): measure, do not assume, applies to assumptions about your own privileges

`docs:check` went red on `main` on 2026-10-10: INCIDENTS.md's "A permission granted to a human,
read as a permission granted to the agent" took a dated `No rule yet` on 2026-09-09, and the
exemption runs out at 30 days. The entry names what was missing — the extension of the rule to
assumptions about your own privileges was stated in the incident and nowhere in PROVING.md, so a
reader routed only to the rule never met it.

PROVING.md's "Measure, do not assume" gains one paragraph saying it, citing the entry, and the
entry's `No rule yet` is removed. Proposed to the operator before editing, per FINISHING.md, and
added to this branch at their choice rather than its own, since every pull request was red on it.

The two counts pinned in `src/cli/rule-citations.ts` move with the prose, because what they count
changed rather than went stale: `RULE_PARAGRAPHS` for PROVING.md from 28 to 29 for the paragraph
added, `UNRESOLVED_ON_PURPOSE` from 12 to 11 for the declaration resolved.

commit.message:
docs(features): clarify feature update and subscription entitlement removal semantics (#615) ## Context OpenAPI guardian check of `features` (full run), compared with lago-api at `cf4af90` and the SDK clients. ## Description - `PUT /features/{code}`: the description now says that the update is partial, that privileges are matched by their code, that the value type of an existing privilege cannot be changed, and that select options sent in the payload are added to the existing ones. The previous text gave no hint, so a caller could expect the payload to replace the privilege list.
Code references (lago-api at cf4af90) - Controller: [`Api::V1::FeaturesController#update`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/controllers/api/v1/features_controller.rb#L61-L69) calls the update service with `partial: true`. - Service: [`Entitlement::FeatureUpdateService#call`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/feature_update_service.rb#L28) skips `delete_missing_privileges` when the update is partial, so privileges left out of the payload are kept. - Service: [`Entitlement::FeatureUpdateService#update_privileges`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/feature_update_service.rb#L66-L85) matches privileges by code, updates only `name`, unions the `select_options` into the existing config, and never assigns `value_type` on an existing privilege. - Service: [`Entitlement::FeatureUpdateService#update_feature_attributes`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/feature_update_service.rb#L61-L64) only assigns `name` and `description` when the key is present.
- `DELETE /subscriptions/{external_id}/entitlements/{feature_code}`: the sentence "The entitlement remains available from the plan" was misleading, because it could be read as the subscription keeping the feature. The text now says the plan and the other subscriptions are untouched while this subscription stops getting the feature.
Code references (lago-api at cf4af90) - Controller: [`Api::V1::Subscriptions::EntitlementsController#destroy`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/controllers/api/v1/subscriptions/entitlements_controller.rb#L40-L54) calls the remove service and renders the remaining entitlements. - Service: [`Entitlement::SubscriptionFeatureRemoveService#add_feature_removal_if_feature_is_in_plan`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/subscription_feature_remove_service.rb#L54-L62) records a removal for this subscription when the feature comes from the plan, so the feature is no longer returned for it. - Query: [`Entitlement::SubscriptionEntitlementQuery#feature_sql`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/queries/entitlement/subscription_entitlement_query.rb#L77-L91) excludes every feature that has a removal row for the subscription.
- `DELETE /subscriptions/{external_id}/entitlements/{feature_code}/privileges/{privilege_code}`: same correction for the privilege wording, which also read as if the subscription kept the plan value.
Code references (lago-api at cf4af90) - Controller: [`Api::V1::Subscriptions::Entitlements::PrivilegesController#destroy`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/controllers/api/v1/subscriptions/entitlements/privileges_controller.rb#L10-L28) calls the remove service and renders the remaining entitlements. - Service: [`Entitlement::SubscriptionFeaturePrivilegeRemoveService#add_privilege_removal_if_privilege_is_in_plan`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/subscription_feature_privilege_remove_service.rb#L55-L63) records a privilege removal for this subscription when the privilege has a plan value.
- `SubscriptionEntitlementObject.overrides` had no description. It now says the object lists only the privileges that carry a subscription specific value, keyed by privilege code.
Code references (lago-api at cf4af90) - Serializer: [`V1::Entitlement::SubscriptionEntitlementSerializer#overrides`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/serializers/v1/entitlement/subscription_entitlement_serializer.rb#L32-L36) keeps only the privileges whose `subscription_value` is set and keys them by privilege code. - Query: [`Entitlement::SubscriptionEntitlementQuery#privilege_sql`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/queries/entitlement/subscription_entitlement_query.rb#L127) sets `subscription_value` from the subscription level entitlement value only.
### SDK drift (spec is right, needs an `sdk-clients-update` run) | Client | Divergence | |---|---| | Python | No features and no entitlements resource at all. [`Client`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-python-client/blob/c3dee54252c75256ece3fbeea63d44e5d880347b/lago_python_client/client.py#L104-L281) exposes every other resource but neither `features` nor the plan and subscription entitlement endpoints, so they are unreachable from Python. | ### Needs human confirmation (not changed) - `EntitlementUpdateInput` marks [`entitlements`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-openapi/blob/51cea6e321c7aef825a3127cec8a8e7e94adfe0f/src/schemas/Entitlement/EntitlementUpdateInput.yaml#L2-L3) as required, but both controllers default it to an empty object ([`Api::V1::Plans::EntitlementsController#update_params`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/controllers/api/v1/plans/entitlements_controller.rb#L94-L96) and [`Api::V1::Subscriptions::EntitlementsController#update_params`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/controllers/api/v1/subscriptions/entitlements_controller.rb#L64-L66)). On `POST /plans/{code}/entitlements` an omitted key therefore removes every entitlement of the plan, because [`Entitlement::PlanEntitlementsUpdateService#delete_missing_entitlements`](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/blob/cf4af904a26cc53fbb56ee7599a407a12b432628/app/services/entitlement/plan_entitlements_update_service.rb#L64-L68) runs on the non partial path. Should the spec keep `entitlements` required to protect callers from that, or follow the code and make it optional?

Paths, methods, path parameters, the `search_term` filter, the pagination parameters, the `subscription_status` filter, request bodies, serialized keys, required flags, nullability, the `value_type` enum and the length limits in the descriptions were all checked against the controllers, services, serializers, the entitlement models and `db/structure.sql`, and match. commit.message:
NAS-144493 / 28.0.0-BETA.1 / Add E2E coverage for Privileges (#14382)

Adds e2e coverage for Credentials > Privileges: adding, editing and
deleting a privilege from the list.

Fixes #14348

## Changes

- **`e2e/tests/privileges.e2e.ts`** (new). Three tests. Each one is
checked on the list row and through `privilege.query`. The API record
holds the roles' wire values and the groups themselves, where the list
only shows labels and a count.
- **Add.** Add opens the form. The test types a name, picks **Readonly
Admin** in Roles and ticks Web Shell Access. Then it checks the row's
Name, Roles (`Readonly Admin`), Local Groups (`0`) and Web Shell Access
(`Yes`), and that the API holds `roles: ['READONLY_ADMIN']`, `web_shell:
true`, no groups and `builtin_name: null`.
- **Edit.** A target privilege and a bystander are made over the API.
The target names a local group that belongs to the spec, also made over
the API. Edit on the target's row drops Readonly Admin, picks Sharing
Admin and ticks Web Shell Access. The record has to keep the same id,
hold `roles` of **exactly** `['SHARING_ADMIN']` (so a role that was not
dropped fails), and have `web_shell: true`. It also has to name the same
gid. The form shows groups by name and resolves them back to gids on
save, so this checks that round trip even though the edit never touches
the groups. The bystander must be unchanged.
- **Delete.** Delete on the target's row goes through the shared
confirm. Its button has to be disabled until the box is ticked.
Afterwards, `privilege.query` is polled until the target is gone. The
bystander's row and record must both still be there.
- **`e2e/fixtures/privileges.ts`** (new). Find, ensure-absent and
ensure-present, keyed on the name. `local_groups` takes gids, the same
as in `fixtures/users.ts`.
- **`e2e/flows/privileges.ts`**, **`e2e/locators/privileges.ts`** (new).
The row tag is `privilege-<name>`. The list uses `mode="inline"`, so
Edit and Delete are icon buttons on the row
(`button-privilege-<name>-mdi-pencil-row-action`). Roles is a multiple
`tn-select`, so `toggleRoles` clicks each option and then presses Escape
to close the panel. The side panel also closes on Escape, so the flow
then asserts that the name field is still visible. If Escape closed the
whole panel, the test fails at that line, not later at Save.
- **`e2e/flows/navigation.ts`**, **`e2e/locators/navigation.ts`**: add
`goToPrivileges` (`link-privileges` under the Credentials slide-out).
- **`e2e/docs/status.md`**: a paragraph on the new coverage. The test
count goes from 151 to 154.

Teardown runs before and after each test. It removes the three
privileges first and the group last, because middleware will not delete
a group that a privilege still names.

No `src/` change. Every element the tests need already had a
`data-test`, and no existing id was renamed.

## Testing

| Check | Status |
|---|---|
| Lint, `e2e:typecheck` | **Not run locally.** The host this was written
on has no Node toolchain, so CI is the first place this compiles |
| E2E | **Not run locally.** It needs a browser and a TrueNAS appliance,
and the host has neither. This PR touches `e2e/**`, so the E2E workflow
runs it |
| Line length (120) | Checked on every changed `.ts` file |
| Review before push | The shared reviewer could not run on the host, so
a subagent applied the same rubric instead. That is weaker evidence than
the check. Round 1 found one BLOCKER: `labels[0]` was `string \|
undefined` under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. `toggleRoles` now takes a
non-empty tuple. Round 2 found nothing at any severity. It checked every
locator against the template that emits it |

**Unconfirmed until CI runs:**
- Two things about the multiple `tn-select`: that its option ids are
keyed by label like a single select's (`option-roles-readonly-admin`),
and that its panel stays open between clicks and closes on Escape
without closing the side panel. The library source is not on that host.
- That the `@truenas/api-client` v27 types accept the role literals in
`privilege.create`.

## Not changed

- `fixtures/users.ts` still queries and deletes its own privilege inline
instead of calling the new `findPrivilege` / `ensurePrivilegeAbsent`.
Switching it over would touch the sign-in suite, which this ticket does
not cover.

## Not covered

Picking a group in the form, since its chip autocomplete's option ids
could not be checked on that host. Also not covered: directory-service
groups, the Enable DS Authentication prompt, built-in privileges, and
the search.
